title: Absolute zero is the theoretical point of no molecular motion, and it is not reached in practice
summary: On the kelvin scale, zero is absolute zero, the theoretical point where molecules would have no motion that makes thermal energy, and OpenStax says that point is not reached in practice.
body: OpenStax Physics says the kelvin scale is an absolute temperature scale, so the theoretically lowest temperature is set at zero. Zero on that scale is absolute zero, theoretically the point at which there is no molecular motion to produce thermal energy. The page says absolute zero is possible in theory and cannot be reached in practice. It mentions a laboratory low at Helsinki and colder places in nature as comparisons, without treating them as zero. NIST's page already says 0 kelvin is commonly called absolute zero, and the fixed Boltzmann constant is on the linked card. Those defining digits are not repeated. This card is the textbook's no-motion reading and the practical limit.
